accuracy_findings.problem: Mobilized workforce is not capped at the workforce. Buildings can mobilize more than the system has, which is exactly the case the page's own Over-mobilization section describes. "Part of it" contradicts that section.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1518-1532 compute_used_workforce adds up building.workforce for every :built/:damaged tile with no cap. stellar_system.ex:1334-1337 handles used_workforce > workforce.
accuracy_findings.fix: Say "Buildings mobilize workforce." (or "Buildings use it.") without "part of".

accuracy_findings.claim: Each building mobilizes a fixed workforce, the same at every level.
accuracy_findings.problem: The "same at every level" part is true: workforce is a per-building field, not a per-level one. But four housing buildings mobilize 0, and their card hides the MOBILIZED line (BuildingCard.vue v-show buildingData.workforce > 0). A reader could think every building mobilizes something.
accuracy_findings.evidence: Script tmp/help-review/workforce-acc-r0-check.exs on RC.Help.Data.buildings(:slow) found workforce 0 buildings: [:hab_open, :hab_dome, :hab_open_poor, :hab_open_rich]. The others range from 1 to 6 (hypergate 10 is excluded scope). The Megapolis (infra_open) has 2, which matches the '2 MOBILIZED' shot. Data.Game.Building has field(:workforce, integer()) at building level.
accuracy_findings.fix: Add a few words, for example: "Each building mobilizes a fixed workforce, the same at every level. Some buildings mobilize none."

accuracy_findings.problem: The readout's tooltip uses the UI's own words: the title is "Population" and the rows are "Mobilized" and "Total" (galaxy.system.population.workforce / workforce_mobilized / workforce_total). The UI never labels this readout "workforce". The leaf shape asks for the UI's words.
accuracy_findings.evidence: Population.vue:44-54 renders the resource-detail with title $t('galaxy.system.population.workforce') = "Population" and reasons workforce_mobilized = "Mobilized" and workforce_total = "Total" (game.json lines 498-500). The mark itself is correct: x 0.03-0.30, y 0.55-0.83 sits over the '2/15' box.
accuracy_findings.fix: Use UI tokens in the caption, for example "{ui:galaxy.system.population.workforce_mobilized} and {ui:galaxy.system.population.workforce_total} workforce." Or add one sentence saying the game labels this readout Population.

accuracy_findings.claim: List 'Which buildings mobilize:' includes 'A building under construction mobilizes nothing until it is finished.' and 'Demolishing a building frees its workforce at once.'
accuracy_findings.problem: Both statements are correct. Under construction the tile is :empty with :new, and remove_building runs compute_bonus straight away. But they sit under a heading for buildings that DO mobilize, so the list reads inconsistently.
accuracy_findings.evidence: tile.ex plan_building keeps building_status :empty. put_building sets :built, and add_production (stellar_system.ex:1161-1196) then calls compute_bonus, which recomputes used workforce. remove_building (stellar_system.ex ~548-575) calls compute_bonus right away.
accuracy_findings.fix: Keep the three items that mobilize in the list, and move the construction and demolition statements to one or two sentences after it.

clarity_findings.claim: "Each building mobilizes a fixed workforce, the same at every level." says the same thing twice ("fixed" and "the same at every level" are redundant restatements of one fact).
clarity_findings.problem: Minor redundancy makes the sentence feel padded rather than crisp, though it stays well under the 25-word cap and has no lint warning.
clarity_findings.fix: Tighten to one clause, e.g. "Each building mobilizes a fixed workforce, at every level." or "A building's workforce cost never changes with its level."

clarity_findings.claim: The bullet "A damaged building, even though it gives no bonuses." breaks the parallel pattern of the other four bullets (which each just name a building state that still mobilizes workforce) by adding an aside about bonuses.
clarity_findings.problem: A reader scanning the list for "which states mobilize workforce" hits an unrelated fact about bonuses mid-list, which is a small stumble even though the underlying fact may be worth stating somewhere.
clarity_findings.fix: Either drop the "even though it gives no bonuses" clause here (it's system-penalties/building territory) or move it to its own one-sentence edge-case note per the leaf shape's step 5.

clarity_findings.claim: The lone "## Over-mobilization" heading sits over a single paragraph, one indented example, and one closing sentence.
clarity_findings.problem: For a leaf this short (~107 prose words, well under the 180-word cap), the extra heading adds visual weight without much navigational benefit, slightly working against "headings only where needed" from the leaf-page shape in 3.2.
clarity_findings.fix: Consider dropping the heading and letting the over-mobilization paragraph follow directly after the bullet list, since the page has no other sections to distinguish it from.

votes.reason: The mechanic (workforce = population rounded down, buildings mobilize a fixed amount, over-mobilization cuts output) comes through, but the formula's code-block styling and an under-labeled screenshot caption cause a couple of small stumbles.
stumbles: "penalty = 1 − workforce ÷ mobilized" is dropped into a <pre><code> block, reading like a raw dev formula rather than plain player text
The caption "Mobilized workforce and total workforce." doesn't say which of the two numbers in the screenshot (2 or 15) is which
"Tooltips show it as Over-mobilized population." swaps in the word "population" for "workforce" without restating they're the same thing

votes.reason: Clear single read overall — the mobilization rule and over-mobilization formula are both stated plainly with a worked example, and the two screenshots' highlights land exactly on the numbers the captions describe.
stumbles: The page never says which outputs over-mobilization actually reduces — you're punted to "System penalties" for that, so the rule you came for (the % hit) isn't fully actionable on this page alone
"Workforce is a system's population rounded down to whole points" is a slightly clunky phrasing — took a half-beat to parse as "floor(population)"

In the population screenshot, the unhighlighted house (7.5) and smiley (22) icons sit right next to the highlighted 2/15 with no labels — momentary "what are those" before noticing only the boxed one matters
